idiom_name: test-target factory helpers / static samples on the model
implementation_notes: XCTest and Swift Testing provide no fixture factory, so the common form is a helper in the unit-test target: 'enum CustomerMother { static func vip(name: String = "Ada") -> Customer }' or a static sample property on an extension of the model. Structs with memberwise initialisers and default parameter values make simple fixtures one-liners, so the mother earns its place for multi-object aggregates and named business states, while Swift Testing's parameterized tests cover input variation. Keep helpers in the test target only, so shipping code cannot depend on them.
pitfalls: static let fixtures containing reference types (classes, shared stores) are aliased across tests; prefer static func returning a fresh value or restrict samples to value types.
Value semantics do not protect reference-type members: a struct holding a class-based model or store still leaks mutations between tests.
Fixtures compiled into both the app and the test target duplicate symbols and can hide missing imports; add the mother file to the test target only.
Force-unwrapped fixtures (try! / !) crash the whole run and report the failure at the helper, not at the test that needed the data.
